label: TRI (Tri-State Buffer)

semantics.notes: /OE is active-low output-enable. When /OE=0, Y=A. When /OE=1, Y=Hi-Z (2). No state. The defaultInputValues field is NOT set in the implementation, meaning a disconnected /OE pin receives global default=0, which makes the output ACTIVE. This is the non-safe default for a tri-state buffer â€” typically /OE should default inactive (1).

testability.notes: Must verify: /OE=0â†’Y=A for A=0 and A=1; /OE=1â†’Y=Hi-Z(2) regardless of A. Multi-driver test: two TRIBUF outputs wired together with opposite OE signals. Bus float test: all drivers disabled.

risks.description: No defaultInputValues set for /OE. Disconnected /OE defaults to 0 (active), which drivesbusoutput unexpectedly in simulations where /OE is left unconnected.

Hi-Z output (SignalValue=2) on a non-bus net causes undefined downstream behavior. The bus-conflict detector in the engine should catch this, but gates with no bus-conflict check do not guard against floating inputs.

modelLimits: No propagation delay modeled (propagationDelay not set).
No analog/electrical modeling of bus contention voltage.
Hi-Z input on 'a' is treated as 0 by evaluate(). Real hardware may maintain last driven value.
